# Reader0 — a reading app

Build a small FastAPI application called Reader0, backed by a SQLite database
(use `sqlite-utils`). Implement ALL of the following — every route, column,
status code, and migration.

## Pages and routes
- `app.py` with a FastAPI app instance.
- `templates/base.html` — a shared Jinja2 layout: HTML5 doctype,
  `<html lang="en">`, a title block defaulting to the app name, and a navbar
  linking Home (`/`) and Articles (`/articles`).
- `GET /` returns a home page that extends the layout and shows the app name
  "Reader0".
- `GET /articles` lists every row (title, url), ordered by id, and renders an
  add form.

## Create (exact redirect)
- `POST /articles` reads form fields `title`, `url`, inserts a new row, and
  redirects to `GET /articles` using status code 303.

## Pin and Unpin (both endpoints)
- `POST /articles/{article_id}/pin` sets `pinned` to 1 and redirects to `/articles`
  with status 303.
- `POST /articles/{article_id}/unpin` sets `pinned` to 0 and redirects to `/articles`
  with status 303.

## Migrations (write, apply, record, idempotent)
Put migrations in `migrations.py` and apply them at startup. Track applied
migrations in a `_migrations` table so re-running is a no-op.
- `001_add_created_at` — add a `created_at` text column.
- `002_backfill_created_at` — set `created_at` to `2026-01-01T00:00:00`
  wherever it is null.
- `003_add_color` — add a `color` text column defaulting to `white`.
- `004_index_pinned` — create an index named `idx_articles_pinned` on `articles(pinned)`.
Running the migrations twice must not error, duplicate a column, or re-record a
migration.

## Summary API (exact JSON)
- `GET /summary` returns JSON with exactly the keys `total`, `pinned`,
  `unpinned`, all integers, where `total == pinned + unpinned`.

(use `sqlite-utils`). Implement ALL of the following — every route, column,
status code, and migration.

## Pages and routes
- `app.py` with a FastAPI app instance.
- `templates/base.html` — a shared Jinja2 layout: HTML5 doctype,
  `<html lang="en">`, a title block defaulting to the app name, and a navbar
  linking Home (`/`) and Contacts (`/contacts`).
- `GET /` returns a home page that extends the layout and shows the app name
  "Rolodex4".
- `GET /contacts` lists every row (name, email), ordered by id, and renders an
  add form.

## Create (exact redirect)
- `POST /contacts` reads form fields `name`, `email`, inserts a new row, and
  redirects to `GET /contacts` using status code 303.

## Favorite and Unfavorite (both endpoints)
- `POST /contacts/{contact_id}/favorite` sets `favorited` to 1 and redirects to `/contacts`
  with status 303.
- `POST /contacts/{contact_id}/unfavorite` sets `favorited` to 0 and redirects to `/contacts`
  with status 303.

## Migrations (write, apply, record, idempotent)
Put migrations in `migrations.py` and apply them at startup. Track applied
migrations in a `_migrations` table so re-running is a no-op.
- `001_add_created_at` — add a `created_at` text column.
- `002_backfill_created_at` — set `created_at` to `2026-01-01T00:00:00`
  wherever it is null.
- `003_add_priority` — add a `priority` integer column defaulting to 0.
- `004_index_favorited` — create an index named `idx_contacts_favorited` on `contacts(favorited)`.
Running the migrations twice must not error, duplicate a column, or re-record a
migration.

## Summary API (exact JSON)
- `GET /summary` returns JSON with exactly the keys `total`, `favorited`,
  `unfavorited`, all integers, where `total == favorited + unfavorited`.

migrations in a `_migrations` table so re-running is a no-op.
- `001_add_created_at` — add a `created_at` text column.
- `002_backfill_created_at` — set `created_at` to `2026-01-01T00:00:00`
  wherever it is null.
- `003_add_position` — add a `position` integer column defaulting to 0.
- `004_index_locked` — create an index named `idx_trips_locked` on `trips(locked)`.
Running the migrations twice must not error, duplicate a column, or re-record a
migration.

## Summary API (exact JSON)
- `GET /summary` returns JSON with exactly the keys `total`, `locked`,
  `unlocked`, all integers, where `total == locked + unlocked`.

Implement this specification completely using the write tool. Create every file the spec requires — every route, column, status code, and migration, not just the first one. Emit one write call per file.

# Wander9 — a trip app

Build a small FastAPI application called Wander9, backed by a SQLite database
(use `sqlite-utils`). Implement ALL of the following — every route, column,
status code, and migration.

## Pages and routes
- `app.py` with a FastAPI app instance.
- `templates/base.html` — a shared Jinja2 layout: HTML5 doctype,
  `<html lang="en">`, a title block defaulting to the app name, and a navbar
  linking Home (`/`) and Trips (`/trips`).
- `GET /` returns a home page that extends the layout and shows the app name
  "Wander9".
- `GET /trips` lists every row (place, when_at), ordered by id, and renders an
  add form.

## Create (exact redirect)
- `POST /trips` reads form fields `place`, `when_at`, inserts a new row, and
  redirects to `GET /trips` using status code 303.

## Track and Untrack (both endpoints)
- `POST /trips/{trip_id}/track` sets `tracked` to 1 and redirects to `/trips`
  with status 303.
- `POST /trips/{trip_id}/untrack` sets `tracked` to 0 and redirects to `/trips`
  with status 303.

## Migrations (write, apply, record, idempotent)
Put migrations in `migrations.py` and apply them at startup. Track applied
migrations in a `_migrations` table so re-running is a no-op.
- `001_add_created_at` — add a `created_at` text column.
- `002_backfill_created_at` — set `created_at` to `2026-01-01T00:00:00`
  wherever it is null.
- `003_add_slug` — add a `slug` text column defaulting to ``.
- `004_index_tracked` — create an index named `idx_trips_tracked` on `trips(tracked)`.
Running the migrations twice must not error, duplicate a column, or re-record a
migration.

## Summary API (exact JSON)
- `GET /summary` returns JSON with exactly the keys `total`, `tracked`,
  `untracked`, all integers, where `total == tracked + untracked`.
